our_argument_summary: WIN-049 currently rebuts the dome model on K1 (23.93 h) on two independent grounds. First, the physics critique: K1 is the luni-solar diurnal constituent — any model with ~24 h rotation and a moon moving relative to the equator inherently produces K1, and the dome geometry (d/R≈0.13) cannot reproduce the smooth global diurnal-inequality distribution the observed K1 generates. Second, the post-hoc / trivial-transcription critique: both Predicted and Observed values in the dome dashboard are static constants (23.9345 h vs 23.9345 h at 0.01% tolerance), so the dashboard is registering a constant-equals-constant comparison. Verdict: Self-Contradicted.

holes_found.description: Line-number citation imprecision (introduced by the ISS-2861 patch). The current detail_verdict_text cites "(raw-text/08-live-power.txt line 218)" as the source for the quoted comparison "Predicted: 23.9345 h | Observed: 23.9345 h | Tolerance: 0.01%". Verified against the raw-text file: line 216 is "Domain: K1 Tidal Period", line 217 is the Predicted/Observed/Tolerance/Status line being quoted, and line 218 is "Source: IERS published". The cited line (218) is therefore the trailing Source label, not the line containing the quoted comparison. Sibling WIN-046 uses a different but also off-by-one convention — it cites "line 240", which is the Domain header line for S2 (the actual S2 data line is 241). Both citations land the reader inside the correct entry block (a 3-line block), so the substantive point is preserved, but the line-number choice is not consistent between sibling WINs and does not point to the quoted text in either case. A defender could nitpick this as sloppy citation hygiene.
holes_found.recommendation: Change WIN-049 citation from "(raw-text/08-live-power.txt line 218)" to either "(raw-text/08-live-power.txt lines 216–218)" (cite the K1 block as a whole — most defensible) or "(raw-text/08-live-power.txt line 217)" (cite the actual data line). The block-span form is preferred because it also captures the "Source: IERS published" label that is itself probative. Consider applying the same block-span convention to WIN-046 (lines 240–242) for cross-WIN consistency, but that is a separate WIN-046 issue, not a hole in WIN-049.

stronger_arguments.description: A defender might argue that the K1 amplitude at the equator is small enough (~14 cm) that the global-distribution argument is overstated — any model with a moon producing some declination signal could marginally pass casual inspection. The strongest available counter is the diurnal-inequality MORPHOLOGY: K1 is the principal contributor to the daily inequality between successive high tides at mid-to-high latitudes (especially > 30°), which requires a SMOOTH declination forcing distributed across the globe. A near-field moon at 2,534 km altitude (d/R≈0.13) cannot produce the smooth latitude-dependent inequality observed at, e.g., Seattle (mixed semidiurnal with strong diurnal inequality) vs Honolulu (also K1-dominant but very different inequality phase). Citing 2–3 specific tide-station inequality patterns would strengthen the rebuttal beyond what the current evidence text does.
sources: NOAA CO-OPS harmonic constituents tables (per-station K1 amplitude/phase)
Pugh and Woodworth (2014), Sea-Level Science, Ch.4 (diurnal-inequality morphology)

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome model is correct that K1 (23.9345 h) is a real tidal constituent and that any rotating-disc-plus-moving-moon system produces a ~24 h periodicity (data/wins.json:049.detail_evidence). The first sentence of the dome's K1 claim — that a model with a moving moon produces a diurnal tidal signal — is mathematically true for the dome geometry as well as the globe geometry. Recovering the bare period is a low bar that the dome geometry does clear.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Clearing the bare-period bar is not the same as predicting K1 (data/wins.json:049.detail_evidence — "The model has never derived K1's observed amplitude (~14 cm at open ocean) or its global spatial distribution from dome geometry."). The dashboard registers Predicted=Observed=23.9345 h at 0.01% tolerance (raw-text/08-live-power.txt lines 216–218), which is constant-equals-constant. The two failures the verdict actually rests on are (a) the value is post-hoc (Doodson 1921 catalogue, not dome-derived) and (b) the dome's local moon at d/R≈0.13 cannot reproduce the global diurnal-inequality distribution that defines K1 as a physical phenomenon. Period-arithmetic agreement is necessary but not sufficient.

deeper_analysis: The c5→c6 verification cycle illustrates a citation-precision blind spot worth flagging for tinker. The c5 reviewer's recommended citation phrase ("(raw-text/08-live-power.txt line 218)") used the trailing Source-label line number; the decider implemented that verbatim. WIN-046's parallel citation ("line 240") points to the Domain header line. Neither citation points to the line containing the quoted data values. A reviewer reading the patch flow end-to-end — c5 spec → decider implementation → c6 verification — would only catch this mismatch by re-grepping the raw-text file with the exact quoted phrase. The structural fix is for the decider's patch-verification grep (which currently just confirms the line-218 string is present) to additionally verify that the cited line contains text matching the quoted content. Not a blocking issue for this WIN, but a candidate tinker EXP-ID-NNN improvement: "patch verification should string-match the cited content against the cited line, not just confirm the citation string appears." Severity if filed: minor.
